differential_diagnoses.name: Cecal diverticulitis
differential_diagnoses.why: Can present with similar right lower quadrant pain and fever, but imaging specifically identifies the appendix as the inflamed structure rather than cecal diverticula.

differential_diagnoses.name: Mesenteric adenitis
differential_diagnoses.why: Typically presents with enlarged lymph nodes in the right lower quadrant rather than a specific tubular structure with wall thickening and fat stranding.

differential_diagnoses.name: Ureteral stone
differential_diagnoses.why: Can cause right lower quadrant pain, but fever is less typical unless infected, and no hydronephrosis or ureteral stone was seen on CT.

key_findings.fact: Axial CT shows a tubular structure in the right lower quadrant with wall thickening and surrounding fat stranding, consistent with an inflamed appendix.

Coronal and sagittal CT views confirm a dilated, thick-walled tubular structure in the right lower quadrant with surrounding fat stranding, consistent with acute appendicitis. No free air or large abscess seen.
Annotated ultrasound confirms a dilated, thick-walled appendix adjacent to the cecum. A hypoechoic mass (likely appendicolith or inflammatory phlegmon) is noted within or adjacent to the appendix.

uncertainty: The hypoechoic mass seen on ultrasound is likely an appendicolith or inflammatory phlegmon, but definitive characterization would require further imaging or pathology.
